title: A circular queue in an array
summary: front and back chase each other around the array. The % operator wraps them back to cell 0.

checkpoints.text: `front` and `back` both start at cell 0. `front` is the cell to take from, `back` is the free cell where the next item goes.
`A` was stored at `back` (cell 0), then `back` moved on to cell 1.
`J` went into cell 9, the last one. `++back` makes 10, and 10 % 10 is 0, so `back` wraps around to cell 0.
All 10 cells are full and `front` and `back` are on the same cell. That also happens when the queue is empty, which is why the class keeps `numElements` to tell the two apart.
Dequeue takes from `front`: A joined first, so it leaves first. `front` moves on to cell 1.
Enqueuing K. Cells 0 and 1 were freed by the two dequeues, and `back` is at cell 0, so K goes there.
In array order K comes first, but in queue order it is last: C, D, ... J, K, reading from `front` around to `back`. Without the wrap-around, the freed cells at the start could never be used again.
